name: n4_license_info
description: What the station's licence manager says, in one call (one GET of the spy page sysManagers/licenseManager, read-only): host_id; certificates (name, expires, valid); licenses (name, expires, valid, days_left) with license_kind, the qualifier the page gives them (e.g. perpetual); brand, owner and project (the tridium:brand and tridium:about features); maintenance (below); nearest_expiry, the earliest dated expiry among licences, certificates and features (kind, name, expires, days_left, same_date: how many share that date); expired, what is already past (up to 50, expired_count when more); features (count, matched, list of name, expires and attributes by key, capped by max_features, truncated). valid is true only when the page writes the state valid; any other state is valid false with state, the text as written. expires is never, a date (YYYY-MM-DD) or, when the page writes anything else, that text as written with days_left null: such entries are counted in note and are in neither nearest_expiry nor expired. Every days_left counts calendar days from the station's own date (station_date, the day of the SystemService systemTime, which must be a whole timestamp), never this machine's: 0 on the expiry day, negative once past, null for never or when the station date is unknown (station_date_note says why, and expired is null). maintenance is what the licence states of the software maintenance agreement (SMA): sma_attributes, one entry per feature that has sma.* attributes (feature, attributes by key), up to 50 with sma_feature_count; sma_exempt_features, the names of the features whose sma.exempt is true, each once, up to 50 with sma_exempt_count (an exemption of that one feature, never of the licence as a whole); sma_truncated when a list was cut; feature, a feature named after maintenance when there is one; and expires, the end date of the agreement: null unless a local licence file states it, because the page carries none. The page does not carry when a licence was generated nor its version: only when the server was started with --niagara-home NAME=PATH for this station (its Niagara installation directory, reachable from this machine) each licence adds generated and version, and maintenance adds expires, days_left and license from the maintenanceExpiration attribute, all read from the root element of the file of that licence's name under security/licenses and nothing else of it (never its features or signature). Only a regular file of exactly the licence's name is opened; generated_note says, per licence, why the facts are missing: no such file, a link or another non-regular file, a name that differs in letter case, a file over 1 MiB or not a licence, one issued for another host, or past the 100 files read in one call. A local file that matches no licence of the page is neither read nor named. status is ok, not_recognized (the page answered but is no licence manager page), or a spy status: forbidden (the user may not read spy pages), not_found, not_html, parse_timeout; only ok carries the licence fields, so an unreachable page is never an empty licence. A line of the page is read whole or not at all: note counts the lines that matched no known pattern (two entries on one line, a name with a bracket or brace, a heading out of place) and names a cut page, a missing section and a list that was cut. The reply is bounded whatever the page holds: every string taken from the page is stripped of control characters and cut with the marker ...[cut] (200 characters for a name, expiry, state or host id, 64 for an attribute key, 100 for its value), a feature keeps 30 attributes (attributes_truncated), 100 certificates and 100 licences are read (certificates_count, licenses_count when the page has more), every list also stops at a byte budget, and the whole reply stays under 2 MiB for any page up to the 2 MiB read cap. usage (two BQL selects, read-only): one entry per global capacity rule of the tridium:globalCapacity feature, {rule (devices or points), used, limit, headroom, excluded_modules, note?}. used counts as the station's own capacity recount does: every component of type driver:Device (devices) or driver:ProxyExt (proxy points) station-wide, less those whose type's module the licence lists in excludedDevices / excludedPoints (excluded_modules). limit is device.limit / point.limit; null when the licence states none, states no limit, or has no globalCapacity feature (no global limit); null with note when it cannot be read. headroom is limit - used (negative when already over), null when either is null. used is null with note when the count cannot be read or was cut, never guessed. Per-driver sub-group capacity features are not read. plan {add_devices?, add_points?} adds plan_result {fits, over [{rule, by}], note?}: fits false when a named rule would exceed its limit (over says by how many), null when a named rule's count or limit is unknown and none is surely over, true otherwise; an unlimited rule never fails a plan, and a rule the plan does not name is not checked. Without plan the reply carries no plan_result; when the page was not read, usage is absent and plan_result is {fits: null}.

feature.description: List only this feature: an exact vendor:name (e.g. tridium:bacnet), else every feature whose name holds the text; compared without case

plan.description: Additions to check against the global capacity limits: plan_result says whether they fit

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds
